chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
There is no shortening of prayer (qasr) required for the sailors in their ship, nor for the caravan drivers, nor for the camel drivers.

key_terms.الْمُكَارِينَ: Caravan drivers (those who drive camels in groups)

ai.seo_question: Do sailors and camel drivers need to shorten their prayers while working?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that sailors, caravan drivers, and camel drivers are exempt from shortening their prayers (qasr) due to the continuous nature of their work, which negates the standard condition of 'travel' requiring prayer reduction. Scholars interpret this to mean that their workplace is considered their temporary dwelling, or that the constant motion prevents the stability required for the full prayer (tamam) to be obligatory in the same way as stationary residence. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the definition of a traveler's status based on occupational continuity.
